name: Better Stack
description: Better Stack uptime monitoring and incident management: monitors and heartbeats with availability and response times, incidents with acknowledge, escalate and resolve, on-call calendars, escalation policies, status pages and status reports, and the configured integrations.
instructions:
## Better Stack
This connector works with the **Better Stack Incidents API** (formerly Better Uptime, `https://incidents.betterstack.com/api`): uptime monitors and heartbeats, incidents and their timeline, on-call calendars, escalation policies and severities, status pages with status reports, and the configured integrations. Telemetry (logs, metrics, dashboards) is not part of this connector.

**Setup (2 minutes)**
1. Open https://betterstack.com/settings/api-tokens/0, pick your team and copy (or create) a token in **Incidents API tokens**. This team-scoped token is the simplest choice.
2. A **global API token** (https://betterstack.com/settings/global-api-tokens) also works and reaches every team; then pass `team_name` to filter lists, and it is required when creating monitors, heartbeats or incidents.
3. Paste the token into `BETTER_STACK_API_TOKEN` and run `better_stack_list_monitors` to check it. Writes need a token with write access.

**Workflow**
- Is something down? `better_stack_list_monitors` (status `up`, `down`, `paused`, `validating`, `maintenance`), then `better_stack_get_monitor`. Uptime numbers: `better_stack_get_monitor_availability` for a date range, `better_stack_get_monitor_response_times` for the last 24 hours.
- Manage monitors: `better_stack_create_monitor`, `better_stack_update_monitor`, `better_stack_pause_monitor` and `better_stack_resume_monitor` around planned work. Groups: `better_stack_list_monitor_groups`, `better_stack_get_monitor_group`, `better_stack_list_monitor_group_monitors`.
- Cron jobs: `better_stack_list_heartbeats`, `better_stack_get_heartbeat`, `better_stack_create_heartbeat` (returns the ping URL the job must call), `better_stack_update_heartbeat`, `better_stack_get_heartbeat_availability`, `better_stack_list_heartbeat_groups`.
- Incident response: `better_stack_list_incidents` with `resolved: false` for open incidents, `better_stack_get_incident`, `better_stack_get_incident_timeline`, then `better_stack_acknowledge_incident`, `better_stack_escalate_incident`, `better_stack_resolve_incident` or `better_stack_reopen_incident`. Notes: `better_stack_list_incident_comments`, `better_stack_add_incident_comment`. Raise one by hand with `better_stack_create_incident` (alerts people).
- Who is on call: `better_stack_list_on_call_calendars`, `better_stack_get_on_call_calendar` (use `default` for the team's default calendar, `date` for another moment), `better_stack_list_on_call_events` for the shifts in a window. Escalation: `better_stack_list_escalation_policies`, `better_stack_get_escalation_policy`, `better_stack_list_severities`.
- Status pages: `better_stack_list_status_pages`, `better_stack_get_status_page`, `better_stack_list_status_page_resources` (resource ids for `affected_resources`), `better_stack_list_status_reports`, `better_stack_get_status_report`, `better_stack_list_status_updates`. Communicate: `better_stack_create_status_report`, then `better_stack_add_status_update` as things change, and `better_stack_update_status_report` to change the title or reschedule.
- Configuration: `better_stack_list_incoming_webhooks`, `better_stack_list_outgoing_webhooks`, `better_stack_list_slack_integrations`, `better_stack_list_metadata`.

**Before writing**: creating an incident, escalating it and publishing a status report alert real people or public subscribers. Confirm with the user first; set `notify_subscribers: false` for a quiet status report.

**Reading the answers**: JSON:API style: `data` (one object or a list) with `id`, `type`, `attributes` and `relationships`; related users and status updates come in `included`. Ids are numeric strings. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC; date filters (`from`, `to`) take YYYY-MM-DD. Availability is a percentage (99.98), downtime and incident lengths are seconds, response times are seconds. Incident `status` is `Started`, `Acknowledged` or `Resolved`. Monitor passwords, Playwright environment variables and policy incident tokens are left out of the answers.

**Paging**: lists return `pagination.next` (a URL, `null` on the last page); call again with `page` set to the page number in that URL. `per_page` is 50 by default, up to 250; incidents default to 10 and allow 50.

**Errors**: 401 means a wrong or revoked token (or a Telemetry token instead of an Incidents one), 403 a token without write access, 404 an unknown id or an id of another team, 422 a validation error whose `errors` names the field, 429 the rate limit.
prerequisites: A Better Stack account and an Incidents API token (team-scoped) or a global API token.

BETTER_STACK_API_TOKEN.label: API token
BETTER_STACK_API_TOKEN.help: Better Stack, API tokens, Team-based tokens: pick the team and copy a token from Incidents API tokens. A global API token works too.
BETTER_STACK_API_TOKEN.patternMessage: Paste only the token, without spaces, quotes or a Bearer prefix.

verifyHints.401: Better Stack refused the token. Use an Incidents API token (Team-based tokens) or a global API token; a Telemetry token does not work here.
verifyHints.403: The token has no access to this resource or is read-only. Create a token with write access for the write tools.
verifyHints.429: Better Stack rate-limited the requests. Wait a moment and try again.

tools.name: better_stack_list_monitors
tools.description: List the team's uptime monitors with their status (up, down, paused, validating, maintenance), URL, type, check frequency, regions and last check time. Filter by exact URL or name; paged with page and per_page.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

url.description: Only monitors with exactly this URL.

pronounceable_name.description: Only monitors with exactly this name.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_monitor
tools.description: Get one monitor with its full configuration: type, URL, status, check frequency, regions, alert channels, escalation policy, maintenance window and timestamps.

tools.name: better_stack_create_monitor
tools.description: Create an uptime monitor: an HTTP check (status, expected status code, keyword present or absent), a server or port check (ping, TCP, UDP, SMTP, POP, IMAP, DNS) or a Playwright scenario, with frequency, regions and alert channels.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

monitor_type.description: What to check: `status` (any 2xx, the default), `expected_status_code` (one of `expected_status_codes`), `keyword` / `keyword_absence` (text present or absent in the page), `ping`, `tcp`, `udp`, `smtp`, `pop`, `imap`, `dns`, `playwright` (a browser scenario).

url.description: The URL to check, or for server and port monitors the host without protocol. Required for every type except `playwright`.

pronounceable_name.description: Monitor name, read out in phone calls, so keep it easy to pronounce.

check_frequency.description: Seconds between checks: 30, 45, 60, 120, 180, 300, 600, 900 or 1800 (Playwright: 60 up to 86400).

regions.description: Regions to check from (us, eu, as, au). Empty means all.

required_keyword.description: Keyword to look for; required for `keyword`, `keyword_absence` and `udp` monitors.

expected_status_codes.description: HTTP status codes (100-599) counted as up; required for `expected_status_code` monitors.

http_method.description: HTTP method of the check (default GET).

request_timeout.description: Request timeout: seconds for HTTP monitors (2-60), milliseconds for server and port monitors.

request_body.description: Body for POST, PUT and PATCH checks; for `dns` monitors the domain to resolve.

request_headers.description: Custom headers as [{name, value}]. Sending the list replaces all existing headers.

verify_ssl.description: Fail on an invalid SSL certificate (default true).

ssl_expiration.description: Alert this many days before the SSL certificate expires: 1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 30 or 60.

domain_expiration.description: Alert this many days before the domain expires: 1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 30 or 60.

confirmation_period.description: Seconds to wait after a failure before opening an incident (max 86400).

recovery_period.description: Seconds the monitor must be up again before the incident resolves itself: 0, 60, 180, 300, 900, 1800, 3600 or 7200.

team_wait.description: Seconds before the incident is escalated to the whole team; empty disables it.

sms.description: Send an SMS the on-call person.

email.description: Send an e-mail the on-call person.

push.description: Send a push notification the on-call person.

critical_alert.description: Send a critical push notification that ignores mute and Do Not Disturb.

paused.description: true pauses the monitor (no checks, no alerts), false resumes it.

maintenance_days.description: Days the daily maintenance window applies.

maintenance_from.description: Start of the daily maintenance window, e.g. 01:00.

maintenance_to.description: End of the daily maintenance window, e.g. 03:00.

maintenance_timezone.description: Time zone of the maintenance window, a Rails time zone name such as `Amsterdam` or `UTC` (default UTC).

scenario_name.description: Playwright monitors: the scenario name shown in the dashboard (required for `playwright` on create).

playwright_script.description: Playwright monitors: the JavaScript source of the scenario.

tools.name: better_stack_pause_monitor
tools.description: Pause a monitor: Better Stack stops checking it and sends no alerts until it is resumed. Use for planned work on the checked service.

tools.name: better_stack_resume_monitor
tools.description: Resume a paused monitor: checks and alerts start again with the monitor's existing settings.

tools.name: better_stack_get_monitor_availability
tools.description: Availability summary (SLA) of a monitor for a date range: availability percentage, total downtime in seconds, number of incidents, longest and average incident.

tools.name: better_stack_get_monitor_response_times
tools.description: Response times of a monitor's checks over the last 24 hours, per region, oldest first: the total response time in seconds for each check.

tools.name: better_stack_list_monitor_groups
tools.description: List the monitor groups (the folders monitors are sorted into on the dashboard), with their name, paused flag and team.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_monitor_group
tools.description: Get one monitor group by id: its name, sort index, paused flag, team and timestamps.

tools.name: better_stack_list_monitor_group_monitors
tools.description: List the monitors inside one monitor group, with the same fields as better_stack_list_monitors; paged with page and per_page.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_list_heartbeats
tools.description: List heartbeat (cron job) monitors: name, status, expected period and grace in seconds, the ping URL the job must call, paused flag and group.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_heartbeat
tools.description: Get one heartbeat monitor with its ping URL, period, grace, status, alert channels, escalation policy and maintenance window.

tools.name: better_stack_create_heartbeat
tools.description: Create a heartbeat monitor for a cron job or background task. The answer holds the ping URL the job must request after each run; a missed beat opens an incident.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

name.description: Name of the service sending the heartbeat.

period.description: Expected interval between beats, in seconds (min 30).

grace.description: Seconds a beat may be late before it counts as missed (about 20% of period is a good value).

sms.description: Send an SMS the on-call person.

email.description: Send an e-mail the on-call person.

push.description: Send a push notification the on-call person.

critical_alert.description: Send a critical push notification that ignores mute and Do Not Disturb.

team_wait.description: Seconds before the incident is escalated to the whole team; empty disables it.

paused.description: true pauses the heartbeat (no alerts), false resumes it.

server_timezone.description: IANA time zone (e.g. Europe/Berlin) for DST-aware missed-beat detection; needs a period of at least 3600.

tools.name: better_stack_update_heartbeat
tools.description: Change a heartbeat monitor: name, period, grace, alert channels, group, escalation policy, or pause and resume it with paused. Only the fields you pass change.

name.description: Name of the service sending the heartbeat.

period.description: Expected interval between beats, in seconds (min 30).

grace.description: Seconds a beat may be late before it counts as missed (about 20% of period is a good value).

sms.description: Send an SMS the on-call person.

email.description: Send an e-mail the on-call person.

push.description: Send a push notification the on-call person.

critical_alert.description: Send a critical push notification that ignores mute and Do Not Disturb.

team_wait.description: Seconds before the incident is escalated to the whole team; empty disables it.

paused.description: true pauses the heartbeat (no alerts), false resumes it.

server_timezone.description: IANA time zone (e.g. Europe/Berlin) for DST-aware missed-beat detection; needs a period of at least 3600.

tools.name: better_stack_get_heartbeat_availability
tools.description: Availability summary of a heartbeat for a date range: availability percentage, total downtime in seconds, number of incidents, longest and average incident.

tools.name: better_stack_list_heartbeat_groups
tools.description: List the heartbeat groups, with their name, paused flag, sort index and team. Use the id as heartbeat_group_id when creating or moving heartbeats.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_list_incidents
tools.description: List incidents, newest first: name, cause, status (Started, Acknowledged, Resolved), start, acknowledge and resolve times and who did it, the monitor or heartbeat behind it. Filter by date range, monitor, heartbeat, resolved and acknowledged.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

from.description: Only incidents from this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

to.description: Only incidents until this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

resolved.description: false lists only open incidents, true only resolved ones; empty lists both.

acknowledged.description: false lists only unacknowledged incidents, true only acknowledged ones; empty lists both.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_incident
tools.description: Get one incident with its cause, status, timestamps, who acknowledged and resolved it, alert channels, escalation policy, metadata and the failing response.

tools.name: better_stack_get_incident_timeline
tools.description: Timeline of an incident, newest first: alerts sent, acknowledgements, escalations, comments, status page updates and the captured responses.

tools.name: better_stack_create_incident
tools.description: Open a manual incident and alert the on-call person through the chosen channels (call, SMS, e-mail, push), optionally escalating with a given policy.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

requester_email.description: E-mail of the team member reporting the incident (required with an API token).

summary.description: Brief summary, sent in the alerts.

sms.description: Send an SMS the on-call person.

email.description: Send an e-mail the on-call person.

push.description: Send a push notification the on-call person.

critical_alert.description: Send a critical push notification that ignores mute and Do Not Disturb.

team_wait.description: Seconds before the incident is escalated to the whole team; empty disables it.

policy_id.description: Escalation policy id to escalate with, from `better_stack_list_escalation_policies`.

tools.name: better_stack_acknowledge_incident
tools.description: Acknowledge an ongoing incident: further escalation stops while the incident stays open until it is resolved.

acknowledged_by.description: E-mail or name of who acknowledges it (shown in the timeline).

tools.name: better_stack_resolve_incident
tools.description: Resolve an ongoing incident. A monitor that is still failing opens a new incident on its next check.

resolved_by.description: E-mail or name of who resolves it (shown in the timeline).

tools.name: better_stack_reopen_incident
tools.description: Reopen a resolved incident, for example when the problem came back right after it was marked as resolved.

reopened_by.description: E-mail or name of who reopens it (shown in the timeline).

tools.name: better_stack_escalate_incident
tools.description: Escalate an ongoing incident to a team member, a team, an on-call calendar, an escalation policy or the whole organization, choosing the alert channels.

user_email.description: For User: the team member's e-mail.

schedule_id.description: For Schedule: on-call calendar id from `better_stack_list_on_call_calendars`.

policy_id.description: For Policy: escalation policy id from `better_stack_list_escalation_policies`.

call.description: Phone call (User, Team, Schedule or Organization).

sms.description: Send an SMS (User, Team, Schedule or Organization).

email.description: Send an e-mail (User, Team, Schedule or Organization).

push.description: Send a push notification (User, Team, Schedule or Organization).

critical_alert.description: Send a critical push notification that ignores mute and Do Not Disturb.

escalated_by.description: E-mail or name of who escalates it (shown in the timeline).

tools.name: better_stack_list_incident_comments
tools.description: List the comments posted on an incident, with their text (Markdown), author and timestamps.

tools.name: better_stack_add_incident_comment
tools.description: Post a comment on an incident, for example a status note or the root cause; it appears in the incident timeline.

user_email.description: E-mail of a team member to tag in the comment.

tools.name: better_stack_list_on_call_calendars
tools.description: List on-call calendars (schedules) with their name, team and whether each is the team's default, plus who is on call right now.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_on_call_calendar
tools.description: Who is on call on a calendar, now or at a given date and time: names, e-mails, phone numbers and holiday status of the on-call users.

schedule_id.description: On-call calendar id from `better_stack_list_on_call_calendars`, or `default` for the team's default calendar.

date.description: ISO 8601 date or date-time to see who is on call then; empty means now.

tools.name: better_stack_list_on_call_events
tools.description: List the shifts of an on-call calendar in a time window: who is on call (e-mails), start and end time, and whether the shift is an override.

schedule_id.description: On-call calendar id from `better_stack_list_on_call_calendars`, or `default` for the team's default calendar.

starts_at.description: Only shifts starting at or after this ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z.

ends_at.description: Only shifts ending at or before this ISO 8601 date-time.

tools.name: better_stack_list_escalation_policies
tools.description: List escalation policies with their steps (who is alerted, after how many minutes, with which severity), repeat settings and fallback policy.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_escalation_policy
tools.description: Get one escalation policy with its ordered steps, step members (users, on-call, Slack, webhooks), wait times, repeat count and fallback policy.

tools.name: better_stack_list_severities
tools.description: List the severities (urgencies) of the team, with the alert channels each one uses (call, SMS, e-mail, push, critical alert). Escalation policy steps refer to them.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_list_status_pages
tools.description: List the status pages: company name, subdomain and custom domain, published flag, overall state (operational, degraded, downtime, maintenance), time zone and settings.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_status_page
tools.description: Get one status page with its domain, overall state, published and subscribable flags, history length, design and access settings.

tools.name: better_stack_list_status_page_resources
tools.description: List the resources shown on a status page (monitors, heartbeats, groups) with their public name, current status, availability and daily status history. The ids go into affected_resources of status reports.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_list_status_reports
tools.description: List the status reports (incident announcements and maintenance windows) on a status page with title, type, start and end, affected resources and overall state.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_get_status_report
tools.description: Get one status report on a status page with its type, start and end, affected resources, overall state and its status updates (in `included`).

tools.name: better_stack_create_status_report
tools.description: Publish a status report on a public status page: an incident announcement or a planned maintenance, with the affected resources and a first message. Subscribers are e-mailed unless notify_subscribers is false.

title.description: Title of the report shown on the status page.

message.description: Text of the first status update.

report_type.description: `manual` (default) for an incident announcement, `maintenance` for planned maintenance.

affected_resources.description: Resources shown as affected: [{status_page_resource_id, status}], ids from `better_stack_list_status_page_resources`. Status is `degraded`, `downtime` or `resolved` (`maintenance` or `not_affected` for maintenance reports).

notify_subscribers.description: E-mail the status page subscribers (default true).

published_at.description: ISO 8601 time shown for the first update (default now).

starts_at.description: Maintenance only: ISO 8601 start of the maintenance (default now).

ends_at.description: ISO 8601 end; required for maintenance, not before starts_at.

tools.name: better_stack_update_status_report
tools.description: Change a status report's title or its start and end time, for example to reschedule a maintenance. To post news, use better_stack_add_status_update.

ends_at.description: New ISO 8601 end time (reschedules a maintenance end).

tools.name: better_stack_list_status_updates
tools.description: List the status updates posted on a status report, with message, publish time, affected resources and whether subscribers were notified.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_add_status_update
tools.description: Post a new update on a status report, e.g. investigating, identified, monitoring or resolved; set every affected resource to `resolved` to close the report.

affected_resources.description: Resources shown as affected: [{status_page_resource_id, status}], ids from `better_stack_list_status_page_resources`. Status is `degraded`, `downtime` or `resolved` (`maintenance` or `not_affected` for maintenance reports).

notify_subscribers.description: E-mail the status page subscribers (default true).

published_at.description: ISO 8601 time shown for the update (default now).

tools.name: better_stack_list_incoming_webhooks
tools.description: List the incoming webhook integrations that open and resolve incidents from other tools, with their name, URL and the rules for starting and resolving incidents.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_list_outgoing_webhooks
tools.description: List the outgoing webhook integrations that Better Stack calls on incident and monitor events, with their name, target URL and triggers.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_list_slack_integrations
tools.description: List the Slack integrations of the team: workspace, channel and the kinds of notifications sent there.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.

tools.name: better_stack_list_metadata
tools.description: List metadata records (key and values) attached to monitors, heartbeats, incidents and integrations, e.g. service owner or environment; filter by owner type and id.

team_name.description: Only with a global API token: the team name to filter by (or, on create, the team that owns the new resource). Leave empty with a team-scoped Incidents API token.

owner_type.description: Only metadata of this resource type.

owner_id.description: Only metadata of this resource id (use with owner_type).

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Take it from the `page` value in `pagination.next`.
